_why: Which gate jobs prove they reached their measuring phase, and which are exempt.
#1509's second-order defect: `corpus-drift` failed for days at SETUP — the poisoned pipx cache
killed it before it scored a single baseline — and produced nothing distinguishable from 'ran and
found no drift'. In that window PR #1447 merged on three green required checks while the gate that
measures its blast radius had never executed. 653 M5-slop findings were silently suppressed and a
live regression reached `main`.
So every job here emits a receipt naming HOW MANY UNITS it scored, after it scored them, and
asserts that receipt before it is allowed to be green — src/audit-runner.ts's `Examined` rule
(unitsExamined: 0 is a NotAssessed, never a clean scan) applied to CI. Mechanism:
.github/actions/gate-liveness. Design note: docs/design/ci-gate-liveness.md.
THIS FILE IS THE FAIL-LOUD PART. src/ci-liveness.test.ts (under `pnpm verify`) holds it to four
rules, and requires every gate id here to be BOTH asserted by its workflow and produced by
something (a `gate:` record step, or recordMeasured/recordDeclaredNoOp in a gate CLI). A new gate
cannot quietly join without one, and a producer/asserter mismatch is a test failure rather than a
silently vacuous check.
#1568 (2026-07-31) replaced the DISCOVERY rule. It used to require registration only of workflows
that install the mechanical binaries — a PROXY for 'heavy enough to die in setup', chosen because
that is what #1509 broke, and it left NINE workflows outside the registry by construction. The
rule is now EXHAUSTIVE over .github/workflows/*.yml: every file is a `gates` row or an `exempt`
row, so a new workflow cannot be omitted, only classified. Measured on adoption: the proxy also
missed semantic-freshness.yml and site-ci.yml, which #1568's own list of nine did not name — the
shape a proxy cannot fix by being widened.
AN EXEMPTION IS A CLAIM, and this one is machine-checked rather than taken on the prose. An
`exempt` row asserts that a run which died before scoring is DISTINGUISHABLE without a receipt,
and the test refuses it for any workflow that carries a step gated on an in-job filter output or
a matrix conditional — that is exactly the shape (#1107's `paths:`-filter-moved-in-job) which
turns a dead scoring phase GREEN. Every exempt row therefore states two things separately:
`measures` (what the job scores) and `whyDistinguishable` (what a reader sees when it dies).
#1569 (2026-07-31): a guard nobody has watched fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot,
so every gate carries `provenBy` — the workflow_dispatch run that FORCED its scoring off and
watched the assert be the only failing step — or the `pendingProof` hatch, mirroring
.github/alert-paths.json. Re-prove any of them with:
gh workflow run "<workflow name>" -f liveness_drill=true
MEASURED 2026-07-31 (alert-paths.yml's own header records the same): a workflow_dispatch input
need only exist on the BRANCH being dispatched, not on the default branch — only the workflow
FILE must be on main — so a drill is taken before merge, not one merge late.
The liveness drill and the alert drill are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE by construction: each switches the
other's machinery off. `alert_drill` skips the liveness assert (it fails on purpose before
anything is scored); `liveness_drill` skips the alert step, because otherwise proving the guard
under workflow_dispatch would open a REAL tracking issue indistinguishable from a genuine failure
— which is why #1586's criterion 4 sat unproven rather than being dispatched.

gates.note: One record per corpus-drift invocation; the #1498 narrowed-PR path emits one per scored target and the assert sums them.

Two gates because the negative controls are a separate claim: a gate nobody has watched fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot, so 'the controls ran' must be asserted, not inferred from the steps existing.
Regeneration and comparison are separate phases. A regeneration that produced findings and then never got diffed is exactly the produce-vs-deliver gap CLAUDE.md's conservation rule is about.

heavy-cli, sharded 1..3. calibration-gate is shard 1 only and source-recall-gate shard 2 only and m2-coverage-gate shard 3 only (#1483), so the assert's `expect` is matrix-dependent — a `if: matrix.shard == N` step that stops matching would otherwise vanish in silence.
Monthly, so a dead run is invisible for 30 days. The CLI already refuses a zero-entry score; the receipt is what makes the fetch/lockfile-tree/osv phases upstream of it equally loud.

Monthly over five THIRD-PARTY clones, so a run that dies in setup or in the fetch phase is invisible for 30 days. The CLI already refuses a zero-target score; the receipt covers every phase upstream of it. Added because the registry check FAILED LOUD on this workflow the moment #1185 landed it on main — the mechanism working exactly as designed.

#1568. Gate 4 and gate 4b share one job and one in-job filter, so a filter that stopped matching would retire BOTH in a green run. Two ids because they score different populations — semgrep rules read for a comment-declared bound, and modules with sibling scan paths — and one id would let either stand in for the other.

#1568. The marker-label pass is the one assertion in this repo NO DIFF CAN SPEAK TO, so a run that died before reaching it reports an absence that reads exactly like 'every label exists'. The three seeded controls are a separate claim and sit behind the in-job filter, so they get their own id and their own declared no-op.

#1568. `acceptance-pr` rides inside `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, so the assert's `expect` is EVENT-dependent the way ci.yml's is matrix-dependent. The self-test is the gate's negative control and is its own claim.

#1568, and the sharpest case in the registry: this job runs on `issues: [closed]`. It answers to no PR, it is on no schedule and it raises no alarm, so a run that dies in setup posts no comment, re-opens nothing, and is indistinguishable from a close it had no objection to. `acceptance-close` records a DECLARED NO-OP on the bot-issue exemption rather than a count, because 'not assessed on purpose' and 'never got there' must not share a channel.

#1545. Daily, and its live half does not run on a pull_request, so the assert's `expect` is EVENT-dependent the way ci.yml's is matrix-dependent. `supervised-declines` records a DECLARED NO-OP on a window with no merged PRs, because 'nothing merged' and 'never reached `gh pr list`' must not share an empty receipt.

pendingProof.why: The workflow FILE is not yet on the default branch, and GitHub refuses workflow_dispatch for one that is not — MEASURED 2026-07-31 from the branch that declares it: `gh api .../workflows/supervised-declines.yml/dispatches` returned HTTP 404 while ten sibling drills dispatched from the SAME branch the same hour all ran. This is the file-not-on-main case, not the input-not-on-main one that #1333 falsified.

exempt.measures: Re-runs every empirical falsifier in the recorded-reason registry (`validate-reasons --revalidate`) and re-tests the external-corpus not-run reasons, daily.
exempt.whyDistinguishable: Every step runs unconditionally — no in-job filter, no matrix, no `continue-on-error` — so a run that dies before the revalidation pass exits NON-ZERO, and its own `ci-reasons-alert` path then find-or-updates a tracking issue on a schedule failure. The absence is therefore already loud in two places. What it does NOT cover: a falsifier that runs and cannot fire (#1345's case-sensitive `grep -q CLOSED`), which is a property of the falsifier, not of this job's liveness.

exempt.measures: Runs Stryker mutation scoring per pinned corpus target against its committed baseline — the tier corpus-drift explicitly defers (#470).
exempt.whyDistinguishable: No conditional step and no failure-swallowing: a run that dies before Stryker exits non-zero and its `ci-corpus-m8-alert` path opens or updates a tracking issue. A partial run cannot report as clean either — the scorer fails on a target whose mutation run produced no report, rather than scoring it zero.

exempt.measures: Reads the external OSV database's freshness and fails when the pinned advisory data has gone stale past its window.
exempt.whyDistinguishable: Every step runs unconditionally, and the check's own failure mode IS an unreadable database — a fetch that cannot complete exits non-zero rather than reporting a fresh result, and `ci-osv-staleness-alert` raises it. There is no green-having-read-nothing state for a receipt to disclose.

exempt.measures: Reads the state of the two upstream OWASP cheat-sheet proposals (#2308/#2309) and reports a change once, stamping the last-reported state into its own tracking issue.
exempt.whyDistinguishable: Its two `exit 0` paths are BOTH downstream of the read — 'no change' and 'already reported' — so they are outcomes of a completed measurement, not short-circuits around it. #1402 deliberately removed the one shape that could exit 0 having silently dropped a read, and a failed read now turns the job red where `ci-owasp-watch-alert` picks it up.

exempt.measures: Checks that the recorded M1-semantic pass artifacts have not gone stale against the corpus they were scored on.
exempt.whyDistinguishable: No conditional scoring step, and it carries a `ci-semantic-freshness-alert` path that find-or-updates a tracking issue on a scheduled failure — so a run that dies before the freshness read is red AND alarmed, never a quiet green.

exempt.measures: Fetches the deployed marketing site and asserts the live pages and the quote path respond as expected.
exempt.whyDistinguishable: Nothing here short-circuits: a fetch that fails IS the failure this job exists to report, so a dead run and a bad result take the same red path, and `site-smoke-alert` raises it on a schedule. A receipt would restate the job's own verdict.

exempt.measures: Builds and lints `site/` on any PR that touches it — `next build` catches what `tsc --noEmit` does not.
exempt.whyDistinguishable: It reports on the PR that caused it, so a run that dies in setup is a RED check the author sees before merging. There is no cadence over which its silence could accumulate unread, and no in-job filter that could make a dead build green.
